evidence.text: For babies who are being treated with intravenous antibiotics because of risk factors for early-onset infection or clinical indicators of possible infection, stop antibiotics at 36 hours if: • the blood culture is negative and • the initial clinical suspicion of infection was not strong and • the baby's clinical condition is reassuring, with no clinical indicators of possible infection (see box 2 for clinical indicators of possible early-onset infection) and • the levels and trends of C-reactive protein concentration are reassuring. [2012, amended 2026]

reasons: The claim states that a negative culture at 36 hours guarantees antibiotics can be stopped even with ongoing respiratory distress. The guideline (E1) specifies that stopping antibiotics at 36 hours requires multiple conditions: negative culture, low initial suspicion, a reassuring clinical condition, and reassuring CRP trends. Ongoing respiratory distress means the clinical condition is not reassuring, so the claim is not supported and is contradicted by the source.

The guideline requires multiple conditions (negative culture, low initial suspicion, reassuring clinical condition, no clinical indicators, and reassuring CRP) before stopping antibiotics. The claim that a negative culture alone guarantees stopping antibiotics, even with ongoing respiratory distress, is not supported.
